message.content:
**Answer**

The last common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus quagga*) is the last common ancestor of all **Laurasiatherian mammals** – the clade that contains both the order Carnivora (felids) and the order Perissodactyla (equids). This ancestor lived roughly **90–100 million years ago**, during the late Cretaceous period, before the diversification of the major placental mammal groups. In other words, lions and zebras share a common ancestor that is the same one that gave rise to all modern placental mammals.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The common ancestor of lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) would be a common ancestor in the mammalian lineage. Lions are felids, zebras are equids. Both belong to the order Carnivora? No, zebras are in order Perissodactyla (odd-toed ungulates). So their common ancestor is at the level of mammals, perhaps the last common ancestor of all placental mammals. But maybe they want the most recent common ancestor of the two species, which would be the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae. That would be the ancestor of the clade that includes both families, which is the clade of mammals that includes the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That is the clade of Laurasiatheria? Actually, Felidae is in Laurasiatheria, as is Equidae. So the last common ancestor of Felidae and Equidae would be the ancestor of Laurasiatheria. But the last common ancestor of all placental mammals is older. So the answer: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived around 100 million years ago. Or more specifically, the last common ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria, which lived about 90 million years ago.

But the question might be answered simply: The common ancestor of lion and zebra is the common ancestor of all mammals, or the last common ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria. Provide details: The last common ancestor of Felidae and Equidae is the ancestor of the clade that includes all Laurasiatherian mammals, which diverged from other placental mammals around 90 million years ago. So the answer: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived around 100 million years ago. Or if we want to be more precise: The last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae is the ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria, which lived around 90 million years ago.
